Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

mara: 1) setup notes: bag filled from a low tap, filter attached by hand, clean bottle below the outlet. 2) handling notes: cord loop fit around a 3 cm branch, and the buckle stayed closed while i adjusted the height. i didn’t time a full bottle.

leon: helpful. did you notice any water left in the hose after packing it? we had that question after the last field day, since the zip pouch is pretty narrow and the hose has to curve around the cartridge.

mara: there was a small amount in the lower bend after i disconnected the bottle. i tipped the hose toward the dirty-water end before putting it away, and most of it drained back into the bag. the pouch closed without pressing on the filter.

sam: for the pouch, current dimensions are 19 by 11 cm laid flat. the cartridge and folded hose fit, but the spare gasket was loose in the corner. i put the gasket in its own little paper sleeve so it wouldn’t get lost during the walk back.

jo: thanks, that’s useful. the instruction card in this sample says to backflush with clean water after use, but it doesn’t say how much water to use. the draft card in the shared folder has “a few squeezes,” which may be vague. i haven’t changed either version.

leon: can we keep both card versions in the folder for now and add a comment about the wording? i’d rather have someone check the backflush steps against the cartridge instructions before we settle on a line. no need to print another card this week.

mara: sure. one other detail: the cord is 76 cm end to end, and the slider holds when the bag is full. it’s a little stiff to loosen with cold fingers, though that was after the sample sat outside for around 10 minutes in the shade.

sam: was that the same blue cord as the earlier sample? the photos from april look darker, but the lighting might be different. if you still have the cord tag, could you post the color name here? i’m updating the materials list, not placing an order.

mara: tag says slate blue, lot 24b. i’ve added a photo beside the april one in the project channel. the new photo was taken indoors under the bench light, so it’s not a great color comparison, but the tag is readable.

jo: i saw it. also, the printed logo on the bag is about 4 cm wide and sits 2 cm below the top seam. it didn’t rub off when i wiped the outside with a damp cloth. i didn’t scrub it or use soap.

leon: perfect, thanks. for the next check, i can bring a measuring cup and a timer, and we can record the flow with the same bottle and bag. if the weather holds, i’ll be at the north lot around 9:30 thursday. that’s a plan, not a booked test slot yet.

Next, we check the lumber cart for a piece that is dry and flat. I was going to say cedar—no, maple—for this small shelf, and we mark the cut list on the whiteboard.
